text:
elaine: heads up — support reported a latency surge for DawnProd starting ~03:10 UTC, p95 up ~3x. customer: DawnPay (high volume). Investigating now.
vikram: thanks, putting this on my list. any recent rollouts to that pool?
elaine: last deploy was kernel-selector v2 yesterday 22:40 UTC (canary -> prod). no config changes after that.
maria: I can grab traces if someone posts which host IDs are hitting p95. support-bot: Customer ticket #C-9817 linked: https://support.company/cases/C-9817 (logs attached) :link:
darren: quick glance at logs — a few nodes show increased write stall warnings around 03:08. Not all nodes.
vikram: ok can we run the lightweight repro (100 rps seq-len 512) against DawnProd replica set to reproduce? if it reproduces we can bisect kernel-selector.
tom: I can spin a quarantined job in the perf cluster (job: dawn-perf-1878). will run 500rps to stress KV cache behaviors. ETA 12m.
elainE: @tom thanks. also can we capture flamegraphs + kv cache hit rates? Maria do you have the flamegraph script handy?
maria: putting script here: ```sh
curl -sS https://perf-scripts/run-flame.sh | bash
```
vikram: i want to check if prefix caching caused cache churn — add metric: kv_prefix_evictions and local_kv_misses. Tom, add those to the job.
tom: done. starting now. logs stream: https://perf.company/jobs/dawn-perf-1878
deploy-bot: canary rollout watch: kernel-selector v2 -> 100% (rolled 2026-06-18T22:40:12Z) :white_check_mark:
maria: after 3m run at 500rps I'm seeing p95 ~1.8s up from baseline 0.6s. kv_prefix_evictions spiked by 7x.
vikram: sounds like kv cache thrash. two options: 1) rollback kernel-selector to v1 for DawnProd, 2) tweak cache sizing / disable prefix caching for this tenant as hotfix.
elaine: support wants a mitigation ASAP. customer on standby for a call at 10:30 UTC. any objections to rolling back to v1 for DawnProd?
darren: rollback safe path? will we lose throughput?
tom: rollback is low-risk; it's a config change in router layer and we can target the DawnProd pool only. I can open PR + deploy in the next 8m.
maria: before rollback, quick experiment — if we increase kv cache size by 30% on one node p95 drops to ~0.9s. so tuning helps but rollout of config takes longer.
vikram: given customer SLA, prefer fast rollback for immediate relief, then follow up with cache sizing and kernel fixes.
elaine: agreed. Tom please run rollback canary to 5% first and watch p95 for 10m; if good promote. Support will notify customer.
tom: opening PR: https://git.company/repo/rollbacks/PR-5423 — starting canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by tom: rollback-kernel-selector-dawnprod canary 5% (id: dep-7629)
maria: monitoring dashboard: https://dash.company/dawnprod/p95 — canary up at 03:32, p95 trending down slowly.
vikram: also start gathering perf profiles from before/after to analyze root cause. I'll run kv cache profiler across sample requests and diff heatmaps.
darren: I'm on support call prep. Elaine, can you share the short blurb for customer?
elaine: sure — "We observed a platform change (kernel-selector v2) that increased KV-cache churn for DawnPay traffic pattern. We're rolling back that selector for DawnProd immediately and will follow up with a permanent fix and a postmortem." sending to customer now.
support-bot: Customer notified (C-9817) — they requested an update in 10 minutes and asked for timeline.
vikram: follow-up actions: (1) complete rollback if canary stable (tom), (2) perf bisect kernel-selector differences (vikram), (3) longer-term cache tuning + unit tests for hot-prefix workloads (maria/darren). I'll own the postmortem.
tom: canary looks good at 10m window — promoting to 100% now. dep-7629 -> promoted.
deploy-bot: rollout complete: rollback-kernel-selector-dawnprod -> 100% (id: dep-7629) :white_check_mark:
maria: after full rollback p95 back to baseline ~0.58s on all nodes. KV evictions normalized.
elaine: great work team. I'll mark this as an active incident and schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow 14:00 UTC. please add any logs/notes to the incident doc: https://incidents.company/dawn-kernelselector-rollback
darren: added initial notes and flamegraphs.
vikram: I'll upload diff of kernel selector code paths and propose a safer rollout plan (gradual canary + synthetic hot-prefix tests).
support-bot: Customer updated: rollback completed, latency restored; they requested a follow-up meeting next week.
elaine: excellent. closing async updates here — keep adding findings to the incident doc. :thumbsup:
